newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy product futures end down with soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy product futures end down with soybeans.

text.p: Heavy losses in CBOT July soybeans caused nearby soymeal contracts to end with sharp losses on Wednesday, floor traders said.
Speculators liquidating long positions and commodity fund sales caused July soybeans to end 20-1/4 cents lower.
Soyoil futures also ended sharply lower, but commercial buying in July trimmed losses in that contract, traders said.
"All day long in soyoil we saw commercial buying in the July as the market fell," a floor trader said.
Most of the deferred soyoil months made fresh contract lows during the session.
The soyoil market garnered some support from reports that China purchased 28,000 tonnes of US soyoil for July shipment, traders said.
However, U.S. exporters characterized the sale as a "special one" and said further purchases were unlikely unless U.S. soyoil prices dropped sharply.
Some traders speculated that the sharply lower close in July soymeal would bring end-users to the market.
July soymeal settled down $7.00 per ton at $271.70, and other months were $0.50 to $4.90 lower. July soyoil closed down 0.17 cent per lb at 23.07 and others were down 0.20 to 0.35.
Rumors continued to circulate that some livestock feeders in California were importing up to 50,000 tonnes soymeal from South American sources, traders said.
However, no confirmation of the trade could be immediately obtained from U.S. exporters.
In soymeal trade, ADM bought 400 lots July and Cargill Investor Services sold 300 lots July and 100 August, pit traders said.
In soyoil trade, ADM bought 300 lots July and Cargill bought 500 July and 300 August. Produce Grain bought 300 July and 100 August and Term Commodities bought 200 August.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 25,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 21,078 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 15,000 lots, against Tuesday's 10,237.
